title: Former Global Onboarding Marketing Manager at Twilio Sees Onboarding Complexity as a Bigger Adoption Barrier Than Pricing and AI as a Growth Risk
expert: Former Global Onboarding Marketing Manager at Twilio (left ~18 months ago)
verdict: A former onboarding manager (left ~18 months ago) saw about 27 onboarding steps per product and double-digit trial-to-paid drop-off: adoption friction, not price, was the barrier.

Messaging organic growth (ex-fees): 🔴 **20%–30% of customers trended toward churn each year, only ~30% re-engaged** (estimate, dated tenure); first read, and at odds with 3Q26 organic +15.7% (SB #64174). → Tenet 2 (organic ≥10%) → {c11}
🔴 **~27 onboarding steps per product, double-digit trial-to-paid drop-off**; first read. → Tenet 5 (carrier moat) ↓ {c2}
Voice AI minutes \u00d7 ConversationRela: 🟢 **~20% of trial sign-ups were for voice AI** (estimate); first read on sign-up mix (mgmt: voice AI ~1% of voice minutes, SB #64365, a different measure). → Tenet 1 (AI agent layer) ↑ {c9}

changes: Self-serve revenue **>30% y/y** (hearsay, quoting mgmt) vs mgmt 3Q26 self-serve 30%+ (SB #67665): consistent.
Existing-customer spend **+16% y/y** (hearsay) vs 3Q26 organic +15.7% (SB #64174): consistent.
First read on churn (20%–30% of customers a year trending to churn); no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (AI agent layer): ↑ — ~20% of trial sign-ups were for voice AI.
Tenet 2 (organic growth ≥10%): → — 20%–30% annual churn risk is from a tenure ending ~18 months ago and is not visible in 3Q26 organic +15.7% (SB #64174).
Tenet 5 (carrier moat): → — a double-digit share of customers evaluated alternatives such as Bird, but the expert rated Twilio more reliable.
